prose.summary: Your wooden bedroom furniture meets the rule of origin, so the CEPA rate can be claimed. Claiming the CEPA rate reduces the Basic Customs Duty from 20% to 12.5%, saving an estimated 7500.00 AED on the 100,000 AED shipment. Follow the claim checklist below to obtain the preferential rate.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 94036000, Other wooden furniture, with high confidence. Confirm this code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: The normal (MFN) rate is 20% and the CEPA rate is 12.5%. The estimated saving is 7500.00 AED.
prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff heading (CTH) and at least 40% value addition (VA). The final manufacture check passed, meaning the last manufacturing step occurred in the UAE. The minimal operations check passed, indicating the work goes beyond the simple operations that alone would not confer origin. The CTH check passed because all non‑originating inputs are classified outside heading 9403, and the VA check passed with a build‑down of 52.0% on an FOB basis, exceeding the 40% threshold.

notes.text: The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty only; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge and any anti‑dumping or safeguard duty are still payable.
The agreement refers to box 8 on the certificate, but India's origin rules and certificate form require box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
The '+' in the rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
Factory declared in a free zone: likely not eligible for the ministry's factory registration; confirm with the ministry.
The duty estimate is on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ.
The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
Interpretation: de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
The certificate form discrepancy: the agreement says box 8, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is from secondary sources, not confirmed.
Inference: SWS is charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found).
Inference: anti-dumping and safeguard duties still apply (no exemption found).
